links.outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers to identical RA questions repeated 14 days apart
links.effect: Multiple-choice: 43 (86%) correct at baseline vs 42 (84%) on day 14. Three of seven initially erroneous answers stayed unchanged, four were corrected, and one new error appeared. Binary questions were more consistent than multiple-choice questions.
links.quote: Three of the seven initially erroneous responses remained unaltered.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT clinical knowledge against EULAR RA guideline-based questions
links.effect: 86% (43/50 multiple-choice items) correct at baseline and 84% (42/50) on day 14. Some errors persisted, so knowledge was largely but not fully guideline-concordant.
links.quote: At baseline, 43 (86%) of the multiple-choice items were answered correctly.

screen.reason: The study tests the consistency and accuracy of ChatGPT-v4 on rheumatoid arthritis guidelines across two time points using hypothetical questions, but does not test any specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
